entities.summary:
Al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza al-Yashkurī was a pre-Islamic Arabian poet of the tribe of Bakr, from the 5th century. He was born in the city of Ta’if, Yemen, and was known for his mastery of the pre-Islamic Arabic poetry form, known as the Mu'allaqat. His poem, 'The Scorpion,' was considered one of the greatest poems of the pre-Islamic era and is still studied today by scholars. The poem's use of imagery and metaphor was considered exemplary by later poets, and it is still admired for its beauty and skill. Al-Ḥārith's life is not well documented, and much of what we know about him comes from the accounts of later poets and historians. Despite this, his poetry has had a lasting impact on the development of Arabic literature and continues to be celebrated for its beauty and power.

Al-Ḥārith's poetry was not just a reflection of his personal life, but also a window into the culture and society of pre-Islamic Arabia. His poems often dealt with themes of love, war, and the human condition, and they provide valuable insights into the values and beliefs of the people who lived during that time. The study of his poetry has also been influenced by the desire to understand the cultural and historical context in which it was written.

Al-Ḥārith's legacy extends beyond his poetry, as he is also remembered as a key figure in the development of the Arabic language. His poetry helped to establish the Arabic language as a major literary force, and it played a significant role in the spread of Islam throughout the Middle East. Today, Al-Ḥārith is recognized as one of the greatest poets of the pre-Islamic era, and his poetry continues to be studied and celebrated by scholars and readers around the world.
